events_seen: TRADE (Jul 19): Corbishley receives Michael Wilson (WR, ARI), Tee Higgins (WR, CIN), Breece Hall (RB, NYJ), 2027 R2 pick. Fronge receives TreVeyon Henderson (RB, NE), Kyle Monangai (RB, CHI), Nico Collins (WR, HOU), 2028 R2 pick.
TRADE (Jul 17): Adam receives Justin Herbert (QB, LAC). Fronge receives Jacory Croskey-Merritt (RB, WAS), C.J. Stroud (QB, HOU), 2028 R1 pick.
TRADE (Jul 10): Adam receives Keaton Mitchell (RB, LAC). Wingard receives 2028 R3 pick.
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 21): Drew added Colbie Young (WR, CIN) (dropped Joe Mixon (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 08): Adam added Cyrus Allen (WR, KC) (dropped Phil Mafah (RB, DAL)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 27): Charles added Chris Brooks (RB, GB) for $1 FAAB (dropped Austin Ekeler (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 16): Charles added Matt Hibner (TE, BAL) (dropped Moliki Matavao (TE, NO)).

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: Helix Quant Strategies entered this offseason with a QB void that was, frankly, embarrassing for a superflex roster with championship ambitions. Adam went out and fixed it. I will not pretend the price was cheap. I will not pretend Stroud was easy to move. But the alternative — another season of praying at the altar of zero — was not a strategy. It was a cope. Verdict: executed.

tweets.name: Marty Volkman
tweets.text: Update on the Deepwater situation: the offer Dina confirmed is still on the table, per someone who described it to me as 'still on the table.' Mitchum has not countered, has not rejected, and has not, per my understanding, responded in any direction. The silence is doing something. I'm told it's intentional. I cannot confirm what it's intending.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: Nobody wants to talk about the ForgeHammer RB room so I will. Henderson ran a 4.38 in New England's scheme last year. Monangai is a different profile entirely — short-area, contact balance, third-down capable. These are not the same player. They are not competing for the same touches. In a 0.5 PPR format that distinction is the entire ballgame and Fronge might actually have something here if he recognizes it.

tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: The market spent all of July treating Apex's haul as the obvious winner of that Corbishley-Fronge deal. Meanwhile I noted at the time that Fronge got youth, cost control, and a QB in Stroud who has real upside in a roster built around him. The revisionist takes are coming. They always do. I just prefer to be on record first.

tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Tomorrow's Exchange Report: Marty and Dina are both tracking Deepwater — from two different directions, with two different source pools, and at least one of them is going to be wrong about the timeline. Terrence has thoughts on which one. Eight o'clock.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: Mitchum staying quiet during the most active trade window in exchange history is actually the most sophisticated roster strategy available. I've studied this. Stillness is a form of leverage that seventeen of the last twelve champions have used to great effect.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: Ranking Obsidian's offseason: Brent has Bowers at TE, which in a TE-premium format is basically printing money at one position, and then you look at the rest of the depth chart and the money stops printing very quickly. It's a great painting in a room with no walls. The asset is real. The supporting cast is a mood board.

tweets.name: Big Dog
tweets.text: Genuine question and I mean this sincerely: does anyone in this league actually have a plan for the 2027 class or are we all just treating those first-round picks like a savings account we're too nervous to open? Because Sovereign is hoarding them and the rest of the league is letting him.

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: On the Deepwater offer — I want to add some texture to what's been reported. The hold-up is not the player being moved. Multiple people I trust describe Mitchum as genuinely undecided on direction, not playing hardball on price. There's a difference between a GM negotiating and a GM who hasn't decided what he wants. Right now it reads like the latter.
